text:
maya: Quick Q — I'm trying to pull raw logs for a customer report. I have request_id=0a4f7c and trace_id=4a3b2c. Console trace view shows spans but I don't see a 'raw logs' link. Where should I look? Any quick CLI snippets? Thanks :pray:
aj: If you have the trace id, go Console -> Observability -> Traces, paste the id, open the trace. There's a small 'Logs' button (top-right) that opens correlated logs (it queries by trace_id + any x-request-id). If that button is missing, check the usual suspects below.
devin: Quick CLI options: our internal tool: `rwdctl correlate logs --trace 4a3b2c --limit 200` — returns correlated log lines across services. Fallback: `stern -n prod 'svc-name' --since 1h | rg '0a4f7c'` or just `kubectl logs -l app=svc-name -n prod --since=1h | rg '0a4f7c'`. Stern is the fastest for hunting.
sara: Also confirm the edge proxy header. Look in the trace spans for `x-request-id` or `x-request-ref` tags. If present use that value to query logs because some services only log the header. For example: `rwdctl logs query 'x_request_id:0a4f7c' --raw`.
maya: Thanks — follow up: what if the request id only appears in the request payload (not headers) and the proxy doesn't set a header? I only have trace id.
aj: If you only have trace id, run `rwdctl traces show 4a3b2c --json` — that dumps span attributes; search for any IDs there (x-request-id, client_request_id, span ids). Otherwise you can search logs for span ids: each span has an id attribute (look for `span_id`). Then `rwdctl logs query 'span_id:abcd1234'` can surface the lines.
oncall-bot: Reminder: if logs are older than 7d they may be archived to S3. If you need retrieval ping @storage or open a ticket.
devin: If console seems to be missing correlations entirely, run a replay from the trace store: `rwdctl replay --trace 4a3b2c --output raw` — it fetches raw events associated with the trace from the ingestion pipeline.
maya: I tried stern + the correlate command — I found the edge/nginx logs with an x-request-ref but the backend service pod logs for that request are missing. Any common causes?
sara: Common causes: 1) the pod rotated and logs were archived between the request and your hunt, 2) the service has filtering (only warnings/errors), 3) log agent dropped lines during a restart. Quick checks: look for pod restart around the timestamp: `kubectl get pods -o wide -n prod | rg svc-name` and `kubectl describe pod <pod> -n prod | rg -i restart`. Also check node journal for kubelet restarts: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200`.
aj: If you want I can run a deeper hunt (I have a small script): `rwdctl run-hunt --trace 4a3b2c --include-archived` and attach results. Otherwise paste the console trace link and I'll dig in.
maya: Appreciate it — trace link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/4a3b2c. I'll loop back with the span ids and any headers I find. :thumbsup:
